title: ALLSEER Governance Decision
description: The verdict rendered for an observed event, with the full reasoning chain behind it. This is the system's public product and the record a human reads when asking why an agent was stopped, so it carries the reasoning rather than just the outcome.

action.description: The outcome the enforcement layer acts on.

reasoning.description: The ordered chain of steps that produced this action. What makes the system explainable rather than oracular: a user must be able to follow validation to risk to policy without reading source code.

matched_grant.description: The grant that covered the event, if any.

matched_rule.description: The policy rule that determined the action, or 'default'.

latency.description: Nanoseconds from event receipt to decision. In enforce mode this delay is charged directly to the agent's syscall, so a slow decision path is a usability failure.

enforced.description: Whether the action was actually applied. False means advisory: monitor mode, or an enforcement failure. Critical for audit, since a 'block' that was never enforced must not read as if it stopped something.

verdict.description: within_envelope: matched a grant. outside_envelope: no grant covered it, the core finding this system exists to produce. explicitly_denied: a denial matched, stronger than merely ungranted. constraint_violation: individually granted but exceeded a session budget. grant_exceeded: right capability, wrong target, a different story from a capability never expected at all. indeterminate: validation could not conclude, typically because enrichment failed. Indeterminate must never be silently treated as allowed.

score.description: Normalized to [0,100]. Normalization matters because thresholds are user-configurable, and users cannot reason about an unbounded scale.

factors.description: The individual contributions behind the score. Kept so a surprising score can be traced to its cause instead of taken on faith.

confidence.description: How much evidence backed the assessment. A high score with low confidence is a candidate for human review rather than an automatic block.

name.description: The heuristic that fired, e.g. 'sensitive_path' or 'novel_egress'.

weight.description: Contribution to the final score. Signed: factors may reduce risk as well as raise it.

stage.description: The module that produced this step.
